title: Anorexia of aging and undernutrition in older adults
bottleneck: Aging suppresses appetite through altered gut hormones, reduced taste and smell, poor dentition, and swallowing difficulties, producing protein-energy undernutrition that accelerates sarcopenia, frailty, and immune decline. Yet undernutrition in the elderly is under-screened, and appetite-stimulating interventions have weak evidence.
why_it_blocks: Nutrition is the substrate for every other intervention: exercise cannot build muscle without protein, vaccines work poorly in the malnourished, and wounds do not heal. Ignoring anorexia of aging undermines geriatric care wholesale.
current_state: Screening tools (MNA) exist but are inconsistently used. Protein supplementation helps when combined with resistance exercise; pharmacological appetite stimulants carry risks and limited benefit. Ghrelin mimetics and targeted amino-acid supplementation show small benefits, but no therapy restores youthful appetite regulation and undernutrition screening remains rare in primary care.
